typedef struct fido_cred {
	fido_blob_t        cd;            /* client data */
	fido_blob_t        cdh;           /* client data hash */
	fido_rp_t          rp;            /* relying party */
	fido_user_t        user;          /* user entity */
	fido_blob_array_t  excl;          /* list of credential ids to exclude */
	fido_opt_t         rk;            /* resident key */
	fido_opt_t         uv;            /* user verification */
	fido_cred_extin_t  ext;           /* extensions */
	int                type;          /* cose algorithm */
	char               *fmt;          /* credential format */
	fido_cred_extout_t authdata_ext;  /* decoded extensions */
	fido_blob_t        authdata_cbor; /* cbor-encoded payload */
	fido_blob_t        authdata_raw;  /* cbor-decoded payload */
	fido_authdata_t    authdata;      /* decoded authdata payload */
	fido_attcred_t     attcred;       /* returned credential (key + id) */
	fido_attstmt_t     attstmt;       /* attestation statement (x509 + sig) */
	fido_blob_t        largeblob_key; /* decoded large blob key */
	fido_cred_ea_t     ea;            /* enterprise attestation */
	fido_blob_t        hmac_secret;   /* CTAP 2.2 hmac-secret-mc */
} fido_cred_t;
objects.description: Top-level credential object used for makeCredential. Holds inputs (RP, user, options, extensions) and outputs (authData, attestation, pubkey, etc.).
Decoded extension attributes present in an assertion's authData, including encrypted hmac-secret and credBlob.

typedef struct _fido_assert_stmt {
	fido_blob_t           id;            /* credential id */

objects.description: One assertion statement/result, with the credential ID, user info, extension data, authData buffers, and signature.

objects.description: Pointer type corresponding to the return type of the function declared here. Note: no custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header; only macros and one function declaration are present. This placeholder reflects that there are no user-defined types to document.

Opaque public key type for ES256 (ECDSA over P-256) operations used by the FIDO library. This header only references the type; its concrete definition resides elsewhere (likely in types.h when _FIDO_INTERNAL is defined). Used with functions to allocate, free, convert to OpenSSL EVP_PKEY, and populate from various key representations.

Opaque private/secret key type for ES256 (ECDSA over P-256) within the FIDO internals. Only available when _FIDO_INTERNAL is defined. The actual structure is not defined in this header. Functions are provided to allocate, free, convert to OpenSSL EVP_PKEY, create a new key, and derive a corresponding public key.

Opaque public-key type for the ES384 (ECDSA over P-384 with SHA-384) algorithm used by the FIDO library. This header only references the type; its concrete definition is not present here and is likely provided in an internal header (types.h) or elsewhere in the library. Treat it as an opaque handle managed via the provided constructor/destructor and conversion functions.
OpenSSL’s generic public/private key container type. It is only referenced here for conversions; its definition is external to OpenSSL headers and not provided in this file.
OpenSSL’s EC key type representing an elliptic-curve keypair or public key. It is only referenced here; its definition is provided by OpenSSL and not defined in this file.

Opaque EDDSA public key handle used by this API. The actual structure is not defined in this header; it is only referenced here and constructed/freed via the provided functions. Details of its internal fields are unknown from this file.
OpenSSL’s EVP_PKEY type is referenced but not defined here; it is an external type. Excluded per instructions, but appears in function signatures for conversion.
OpenSSL’s EVP_MD_CTX type is referenced but not defined here; it is an external type. Excluded per instructions, but appears in conditional prototypes.

Opaque type representing an RS256 (RSA with SHA-256) public key used by the FIDO library. This header only declares API functions operating on it; the concrete definition is not present here and is expected to be provided elsewhere (likely in types.h or an internal header).

Opaque device handle type referenced by the API functions in this header. It is not defined in this header; it is expected to be defined in the included FIDO library headers. Details about its layout, construction, and lifetime are unknown from this file.

Metadata about resident keys (RK) on a FIDO authenticator: how many exist and how many more can be created. The full struct layout is available only when _FIDO_INTERNAL is defined; otherwise it is an opaque type accessed via getters.
A collection of relying parties (RP) known to the authenticator’s credential manager. Opaque to external consumers; iterate and query via the provided API functions.
A collection of resident credentials (resident keys) returned by the credential manager for a given RP. Opaque outside of internal builds; access elements via index and helper functions.

Internal-only element type representing a single relying party entry, containing the RP entity and a hash of the RP ID. Not exposed as a public typedef; used inside fido_credman_rp when _FIDO_INTERNAL is defined.

Biometric template descriptor containing an identifier (blob) and a human-readable name. Used to reference and manage a single biometric template on a FIDO device. Note: Full struct layout is only available when _FIDO_INTERNAL is defined; otherwise it is an opaque type.
Container for a dynamically managed array of biometric templates returned by a device query. Fields indicate allocation and population counts. Opaque to users unless _FIDO_INTERNAL is defined.
Holds state and results for an enrollment operation, including remaining sample count, last status code, and an optional token used to continue enrollment. Opaque unless _FIDO_INTERNAL is defined.
Basic device biometric information such as modality type and maximum number of samples required for enrollment. Opaque unless _FIDO_INTERNAL is defined.

Opaque handle for a FIDO2 assertion object. Created with fido_assert_new() and freed with fido_assert_free(). Holds request parameters, results (authenticator data, signature, user info), and related buffers for a getAssertion operation.

Opaque handle for a FIDO2 credential (makeCredential) object. Created with fido_cred_new() and freed with fido_cred_free(). Encapsulates client data, relying party, user, attestation, public key, and options for credential creation and verification.

Opaque device handle representing a CTAP/U2F/FIDO2 authenticator. Created with fido_dev_new() or fido_dev_new_with_info() and freed with fido_dev_free(). Used to open, configure, and communicate with an authenticator.

Opaque container for device discovery/manifest information (path, product, manufacturer, vendor/product IDs). Allocated as an array with fido_dev_info_new(count) and freed with fido_dev_info_free(...).

Opaque structure holding authenticatorInfo (CTAP2 getInfo) data such as versions, options, algorithms, AAGUID, transports, limits, and capabilities. Created with fido_cbor_info_new() and freed with fido_cbor_info_free().

Various referenced typedefs appear in this header but are not defined here (they are likely defined in included headers like fido/types.h). As per instructions, no definitions from this header exist for these; they are listed here only to note absence. Pointer forms shown are placeholders; do not rely on them. If strict adherence requires excluding non-defined types, ignore this entry.

functions.name: fido_strerr
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing a FIDO/libfido2 error code. Intended for converting status/error values (e.g., FIDO_ERR_* and internal negative codes) into messages for logging or diagnostics. Details about exact wording and handling of unknown codes are not documented here and may be implementation-defined.
requirements: Argument must be an integer error/status code, typically one of the macros defined in this header (e.g., FIDO_ERR_SUCCESS, FIDO_ERR_INVALID_COMMAND, or internal negatives like FIDO_ERR_TX).
The returned pointer refers to a read-only, null-terminated string; the caller must not modify or free it (inferred from typical strerror-style APIs; exact storage duration not documented).
Behavior for unrecognized codes is unspecified; callers should tolerate an implementation-defined or generic message (inferred).
Thread-safety and locale/encoding of the returned string are not documented and therefore unknown.

functions.name: es256_pk_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new ES256 public key object (opaque es256_pk_t). Intended as the first step before populating the key via one of the es256_pk_from_* functions or by other library routines.
requirements: Must be called before using the resulting es256_pk_t with other functions.
Caller owns the returned object and is responsible for freeing it with es256_pk_free when no longer needed.
Returns NULL on failure (exact failure modes and errno/last-error behavior are unknown).
Thread-safety and allocator behavior are unknown.

functions.name: es256_pk_free
functions.description: Frees an ES256 public key object and, typically, nulls the caller’s pointer. Accepts an address of an es256_pk_t* so the function can clear it after deallocation.
requirements: The argument must be a valid pointer to an es256_pk_t* (i.e., not NULL), or a pointer to a NULL pointer; passing an invalid address results in undefined behavior.
If the inner pointer is non-NULL, it must point to an es256_pk_t obtained from es256_pk_new or a compatible constructor from this library.
After return, the inner pointer may be set to NULL; do not use the freed object.
It is safe to call with a pointer to a NULL inner pointer (no-op) is typical, but exact behavior is not documented.

functions.name: es256_pk_to_EVP_PKEY
functions.description: Converts an ES256 public key to an OpenSSL EVP_PKEY object for use with OpenSSL APIs. Useful for verification operations or interoperability with OpenSSL.
requirements: Input es256_pk_t pointer must be a valid, initialized ES256 public key; passing NULL or an uninitialized object leads to failure or undefined behavior (exact handling unknown).
On success, the returned EVP_PKEY* is owned by the caller and should be released with EVP_PKEY_free.
Returns NULL on failure (exact failure modes and error reporting mechanism are unknown).
Requires OpenSSL to be available and properly initialized as required by OpenSSL (details not specified here).

functions.name: es256_pk_from_EC_KEY
functions.description: Initializes or populates an ES256 public key object from an OpenSSL EC_KEY. The EC_KEY is expected to carry a P-256 (secp256r1) public key compatible with ES256.
requirements: The destination es256_pk_t* must point to a valid, allocated object (e.g., from es256_pk_new).
The source EC_KEY* must be a valid pointer to an initialized OpenSSL EC_KEY containing a suitable public key; ownership of EC_KEY remains with the caller.
Return value is an int status code; exact success/failure conventions are unknown (commonly 0 for success and non-zero for error, but not guaranteed by this header).
Behavior is undefined if either pointer is NULL.

functions.name: es256_pk_from_EVP_PKEY
functions.description: Initializes or populates an ES256 public key object from an OpenSSL EVP_PKEY. The EVP_PKEY is expected to contain an EC public key compatible with ES256 (P-256).
requirements: The destination es256_pk_t* must point to a valid, allocated object (e.g., from es256_pk_new).
The source EVP_PKEY* must be a valid pointer to an initialized OpenSSL EVP_PKEY with a suitable EC public key; ownership of EVP_PKEY remains with the caller.
Return value is an int status code; exact success/failure conventions are unknown.
Behavior is undefined if either pointer is NULL.

functions.name: es256_pk_from_ptr
functions.description: Initializes or populates an ES256 public key object from a raw byte buffer. The buffer must contain a serialized ES256 public key in a format expected by this library (exact encoding not specified here).
requirements: The destination es256_pk_t* must point to a valid, allocated object (e.g., from es256_pk_new).

The input pointer must reference a readable buffer of length given by the size_t parameter; it must contain a valid ES256 public key encoding as expected by the library. The required format/length are unknown from this header.
Return value is an int status code; exact success/failure conventions are unknown.
Behavior is undefined if the destination pointer is NULL, or if the buffer pointer is NULL while size is non-zero.

functions.name: es384_pk_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new ES384 public key object (es384_pk_t). Use this to create a container for a P-384 (ES384) public key before populating it from OpenSSL types or raw bytes.
requirements: Caller must check the return value for NULL before use (allocation may fail).
The returned object must be released with es384_pk_free to avoid memory leaks.

functions.name: es384_pk_free
functions.description: Frees an ES384 public key object previously allocated (e.g., by es384_pk_new). Takes a pointer-to-pointer so the callee can invalidate the caller’s handle.
requirements: pk must be a non-NULL pointer to an es384_pk_t* obtained from es384_pk_new or an equivalent constructor.
After successful free, the es384_pk_t object must not be used again by the caller.
Caller should assume the pointer becomes invalid; if the implementation sets *pk to NULL is unspecified in this header and should not be relied upon.

functions.name: es384_pk_to_EVP_PKEY
functions.description: Converts an ES384 public key to an OpenSSL EVP_PKEY wrapper. Useful for interoperability with OpenSSL APIs that consume EVP_PKEY for P-384 ECDSA.
requirements: pk must be a valid, initialized es384_pk_t containing a P-384 (secp384r1) public key.
Caller must check the return value for NULL to detect conversion failure.
The returned EVP_PKEY is expected to be a newly-allocated object and should be freed by the caller with EVP_PKEY_free (inferred from OpenSSL conventions).

functions.name: es384_pk_from_EC_KEY
functions.description: Initializes or populates an ES384 public key object from an OpenSSL EC_KEY. Typically used to import a P-384 public key into the library’s native representation.
requirements: pk must be non-NULL and refer to an es384_pk_t allocated/initialized beforehand (e.g., via es384_pk_new).
ec_key must be non-NULL and contain a valid public key on the P-384 (secp384r1) curve (inferred from ES384 naming).
Caller must check the integer return value to determine success or failure; exact return-code semantics are not documented here.

functions.name: es384_pk_from_EVP_PKEY
functions.description: Initializes or populates an ES384 public key object from an OpenSSL EVP_PKEY. Useful when the key material is managed at the EVP level.
requirements: pk must be non-NULL and refer to an es384_pk_t allocated/initialized beforehand (e.g., via es384_pk_new).
pkey must be non-NULL and contain an EC public key on the P-384 (secp384r1) curve (inferred from ES384 naming).
Caller must check the integer return value to determine success or failure; exact return-code semantics are not documented here.

functions.name: es384_pk_from_ptr
functions.signature: int es384_pk_from_ptr(es384_pk_t *pk, const void *ptr, size_t len);
functions.description: Parses a public key from a raw byte buffer and loads it into an ES384 public key object. The specific encoding of the buffer is not documented here; it is expected to represent a P-384 public key (e.g., an encoded EC point) suitable for ES384.
requirements: pk must be non-NULL and refer to an es384_pk_t allocated/initialized beforehand (e.g., via es384_pk_new).
ptr must be non-NULL and point to a buffer containing a valid encoding of a P-384 public key; len must be the exact size of that buffer.
The buffer must remain valid for the duration of the call.
Caller must check the integer return value to determine success or failure; exact return-code semantics and expected encoding are not specified in this header.

functions.name: eddsa_pk_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new eddsa_pk_t public-key object used for EDDSA (e.g., Ed25519) operations. Typical usage is to create an empty key container before populating it via eddsa_pk_from_EVP_PKEY or eddsa_pk_from_ptr.
requirements: Caller must free the returned object with eddsa_pk_free to avoid memory leaks.
Function returns NULL on allocation failure; caller must check the return value before use.

functions.name: eddsa_pk_free
functions.description: Releases and zeroizes (as applicable) an eddsa_pk_t object and sets the caller’s pointer to NULL. Intended to free objects allocated by eddsa_pk_new.
requirements: The argument must be a valid address of a pointer to an eddsa_pk_t (i.e., eddsa_pk_t **).
It is safe to pass a pointer whose referenced value is NULL; the function will be a no-op.
After return, the referenced pointer may be set to NULL and must not be used.

functions.name: eddsa_pk_to_EVP_PKEY
functions.description: Converts an eddsa_pk_t public key into an OpenSSL EVP_PKEY object. Use this to interoperate with OpenSSL APIs that require EVP_PKEY.
requirements: Input eddsa_pk_t pointer must point to a valid, initialized EDDSA public key.
Returns NULL on error; caller must check for NULL and free the returned EVP_PKEY with EVP_PKEY_free when no longer needed.

functions.name: eddsa_pk_from_EVP_PKEY
functions.description: Initializes or populates an eddsa_pk_t from a provided OpenSSL EVP_PKEY containing a compatible EDDSA public key (e.g., Ed25519). Returns a status code (0/non-zero per library conventions; exact semantics not documented here).
requirements: The destination eddsa_pk_t pointer must be non-NULL and refer to a valid object (typically created by eddsa_pk_new).
The source EVP_PKEY must be non-NULL and contain a supported EDDSA public key type.
Caller must check the integer return value for success/failure and handle errors accordingly.

functions.name: eddsa_pk_from_ptr
functions.description: Initializes or populates an eddsa_pk_t from raw public key bytes provided via pointer and length. Intended for loading an EDDSA public key from a byte buffer.
requirements: The destination eddsa_pk_t pointer must be non-NULL and refer to a valid object (typically created by eddsa_pk_new).
The source pointer must be non-NULL and point to at least the number of bytes indicated by the size parameter.
The size must match the required raw key length for the specific EDDSA type supported by this library; exact size is unknown from this header and must be provided correctly by the caller.
Caller must check the integer return value for success/failure and handle errors accordingly.

functions.name: EVP_PKEY_get_raw_public_key
functions.signature: int EVP_PKEY_get_raw_public_key(const EVP_PKEY *, unsigned char *, size_t *);
functions.description: Retrieves the raw public key bytes from an EVP_PKEY into a caller-supplied buffer and sets the length. This declaration appears for LibreSSL compatibility when native support is missing.
requirements: The EVP_PKEY pointer must be non-NULL and contain a key type that supports raw public key export.

The output buffer pointer must be either NULL (to query the required size) or point to a buffer of sufficient size; the size_t* must be non-NULL and on input may contain the buffer size, on output receives the actual size (behavior per OpenSSL conventions; exact details not fully specified here).
Caller must check the integer return value for success/failure and handle errors accordingly.

functions.name: EVP_PKEY_new_raw_public_key
functions.signature: EVP_PKEY *EVP_PKEY_new_raw_public_key(int, ENGINE *, const unsigned char *, size_t);
functions.description: Creates a new EVP_PKEY from raw public key bytes for the specified key type (e.g., EVP_PKEY_ED25519). Provided here for LibreSSL compatibility when native APIs may be absent.
requirements: The type (first argument) must be a valid OpenSSL key type identifier compatible with the provided raw bytes.
ENGINE* may be NULL in typical usage.
The raw key pointer must be non-NULL and point to at least size bytes; size must match the expected raw key length for the specified type.
Returns NULL on error; caller must check for NULL and free the resulting EVP_PKEY with EVP_PKEY_free when done.

functions.name: EVP_DigestVerify
functions.signature: int EVP_DigestVerify(EVP_MD_CTX *, const unsigned char *, size_t, const unsigned char *, size_t);
functions.description: Verifies a signature using the digest/signature verification context (EVP_MD_CTX). This compatibility declaration is included for LibreSSL environments. Typically used after initializing the context with the appropriate public key and parameters.
requirements: The EVP_MD_CTX must be properly initialized for verification with a public key and algorithm parameters prior to calling.

The second argument must point to the signature buffer of length given by the third argument; the fourth argument must point to the message/digest buffer of length given by the fifth argument (exact semantics depend on setup; not fully specified in this header).
Returns 1 for success, 0 for verification failure, and a negative value on error per OpenSSL conventions; caller must check and handle return values accordingly.

functions.name: rs256_pk_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new rs256_pk_t object representing an RS256 (RSA + SHA-256) public key container used by the library. Typical usage is to create an instance, populate it via one of the rs256_pk_from_* functions, use it for operations/conversions, and then free it with rs256_pk_free.
requirements: Caller must check the return value for allocation failure (NULL).
The returned object must eventually be released with rs256_pk_free.

functions.name: rs256_pk_free
functions.description: Releases an rs256_pk_t object and, if supported by the implementation, nulls the caller's pointer. Use this to free objects created by rs256_pk_new.
requirements: The argument must be a valid pointer to an rs256_pk_t* previously obtained from rs256_pk_new (i.e., the address of the pointer).
If the pointed-to rs256_pk_t* is non-NULL, it must not have been freed previously.
Caller should not use the rs256_pk_t object after calling this function.

functions.name: rs256_pk_to_EVP_PKEY
functions.description: Converts an rs256_pk_t public key to an OpenSSL EVP_PKEY for interoperability with OpenSSL APIs. Useful when verifying signatures or interacting with OpenSSL-based code.
requirements: Input rs256_pk_t pointer must be non-NULL and refer to a valid, initialized RS256 public key object.
Caller must check the return value for failure (likely NULL on error).
On success, the returned EVP_PKEY* is owned by the caller and must be freed with EVP_PKEY_free.

functions.name: rs256_pk_from_EVP_PKEY
functions.description: Initializes or populates an rs256_pk_t from an existing OpenSSL EVP_PKEY that contains an RSA public key suitable for RS256 operations. Use when you already have a key in OpenSSL form and need a library-native representation.
requirements: The destination rs256_pk_t* must be non-NULL and refer to a valid object (typically allocated with rs256_pk_new).
The source EVP_PKEY* must be non-NULL and contain an RSA public key compatible with RS256.
Caller must check the integer return status to detect success/failure (exact codes are library-defined; typically 0 indicates success in libfido-style APIs).

functions.name: rs256_pk_from_RSA
functions.description: Initializes or populates an rs256_pk_t from an OpenSSL RSA public key handle. Use when you have an RSA* public key and need to create the library’s RS256 public key object.
requirements: The destination rs256_pk_t* must be non-NULL and refer to a valid object (typically allocated with rs256_pk_new).
The source RSA* must be non-NULL and represent a valid RSA public key.
Caller must check the integer return status to detect success/failure (exact codes are library-defined; typically 0 indicates success in libfido-style APIs).

functions.name: rs256_pk_from_ptr
functions.description: Initializes or populates an rs256_pk_t from a raw memory buffer containing a serialized RS256 public key. The exact encoding format is not specified in this header (unknown; consult library documentation).
requirements: The destination rs256_pk_t* must be non-NULL and refer to a valid object (typically allocated with rs256_pk_new).
The source buffer pointer must be non-NULL if size > 0.
The size must accurately reflect the length of the serialized key data expected by this API (exact format unknown; may be implementation-specific).
Caller must check the integer return status to detect success/failure (exact codes are library-defined; typically 0 indicates success in libfido-style APIs).

functions.name: fido_dev_enable_entattest
functions.description: Enables enterprise attestation on the given FIDO device. Intended for enterprise provisioning/management workflows. The call performs a privileged configuration change on the authenticator and requires authorization via PIN/UV (provided as a NUL-terminated string). Returns a libfido2 error code (0/FIDO_OK on success). Note: enabling enterprise attestation may be a persistent and potentially irreversible change; exact behavior is device-dependent and not specified here.
requirements: The fido_dev_t * must reference a valid, initialized, and opened device handle.
The device must support the relevant FIDO2/CTAP configuration subcommand required to enable enterprise attestation (device-dependent).

The const char * must point to a valid NUL-terminated string containing the authenticator PIN if required by the device; whether NULL is permitted depends on device state/capabilities (unknown from this header).
Callers must check the returned int against libfido2 error codes (e.g., FIDO_OK) and handle errors accordingly.
This operation may permanently change device state; callers should ensure this is intended before invoking (irreversibility is device-dependent and not specified here).

functions.name: fido_dev_force_pin_change
functions.description: Forces the device to require a PIN change by setting the authenticator into a state where the next appropriate interaction will prompt a PIN update. Used for administrative/reset policies. Returns a libfido2 error code (0/FIDO_OK on success).
requirements: The fido_dev_t * must reference a valid, initialized, and opened device handle.
The device must support the configuration subcommand for forcing a PIN change (device-dependent).
The const char * must be a valid NUL-terminated PIN string if the device requires PIN/UV authorization for this operation; whether NULL is allowed is not specified here (device-dependent).
Callers must check and handle the returned int per libfido2 error codes.

functions.name: fido_dev_toggle_always_uv
functions.description: Toggles the device’s "always require user verification" setting (AlwaysUV). Each successful call flips the setting. Useful for enforcing or relaxing per-operation user verification requirements. Returns a libfido2 error code (0/FIDO_OK on success).
requirements: The fido_dev_t * must reference a valid, initialized, and opened device handle.
The device must support the AlwaysUV configuration capability (device-dependent).
The const char * must be a valid NUL-terminated PIN string if required to authorize configuration changes; allowance of NULL is device-dependent and not specified here.
Callers must check and handle the returned int per libfido2 error codes.
The exact initial state and persistence of the toggle are device-dependent and not specified here.

functions.name: fido_dev_set_pin_minlen
functions.description: Sets the minimum allowed PIN length on the device to the specified value. Primarily used by administrators to enforce PIN complexity policy. Returns a libfido2 error code (0/FIDO_OK on success).
requirements: The fido_dev_t * must reference a valid, initialized, and opened device handle.
The size_t argument is the new minimum PIN length; acceptable bounds are device- and spec-dependent and not stated here (unknown exact range).
The const char * must be a valid NUL-terminated PIN string if required by the device to authorize configuration changes; whether NULL is permitted is not specified here (device-dependent).
The device must support configurable minimum PIN length (device-dependent).
Callers must check and handle the returned int per libfido2 error codes.

functions.name: fido_dev_set_pin_minlen_rpid
functions.signature: int fido_dev_set_pin_minlen_rpid(fido_dev_t *, const char * const *, size_t, const char *);
functions.description: Sets the set of RP IDs for which the device’s minimum PIN length policy applies (or is enforced specially), providing an array of relying party IDs and the count. Used to scope PIN policy to specific RPs. Returns a libfido2 error code (0/FIDO_OK on success).
requirements: The fido_dev_t * must reference a valid, initialized, and opened device handle.
The const char * const * parameter must point to an array of pointers to NUL-terminated RP ID strings; each entry must be non-NULL.
The size_t parameter must equal the number of RP ID strings provided in the array; behavior for zero is device-dependent and not specified here.
The const char * PIN must be a valid NUL-terminated string if required for authorization; allowance of NULL is device-dependent and not specified here.
The device must support RP ID–scoped PIN minimum length configuration (device-dependent).
Callers must check and handle the returned int per libfido2 error codes.

functions.name: fido_credman_rp_id
functions.description: Returns the relying party (RP) ID string for the RP entry at the given index within an fido_credman_rp_t collection. Typically used after populating the RP list via fido_credman_get_dev_rp.
requirements: The fido_credman_rp_t pointer must reference a valid, initialized RP list object (e.g., created with fido_credman_rp_new and populated by fido_credman_get_dev_rp).
The index must be less than the number of populated entries reported by fido_credman_rp_count.
The returned pointer is owned by the RP list object; do not free it and ensure the RP list object remains alive while using the string.
Behavior for out-of-range index is unspecified by this header; callers should validate the index before calling.

functions.name: fido_credman_rp_name
functions.description: Returns the human-readable RP name for the RP entry at the given index within an fido_credman_rp_t collection. Use after fetching RPs from a device.
requirements: The fido_credman_rp_t must be valid and populated (e.g., via fido_credman_get_dev_rp).
The index must be < fido_credman_rp_count(list).
Returned pointer is owned by the list and must remain in scope with the list; do not free it.
Out-of-range index behavior is not specified; validate the index first.

functions.name: fido_credman_rk
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the resident credential (fido_cred_t) at the given index in an fido_credman_rk_t collection obtained from a device.
requirements: The fido_credman_rk_t must be valid and populated (e.g., via fido_credman_get_dev_rk).
The index must be less than fido_credman_rk_count(container).
The returned fido_cred_t pointer is owned by the container; do not free it separately and keep the container alive while accessing it.
Behavior for out-of-range index is unspecified; check bounds before calling.

functions.name: fido_credman_rp_id_hash_ptr
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the SHA-256 hash (binary) of the RP ID for the RP entry at the given index within an fido_credman_rp_t collection.
requirements: The fido_credman_rp_t must be valid and populated (e.g., via fido_credman_get_dev_rp).
The index must be < fido_credman_rp_count(list).
Use fido_credman_rp_id_hash_len to determine the length of the returned buffer at the same index.
The returned buffer is owned by the list; do not free it and ensure the list remains valid while using it.
Bounds violations are unspecified; validate index first.

functions.name: fido_credman_metadata_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new, empty metadata object used to query resident key (RK) metadata (existing and remaining counts) from a device.
requirements: Caller must check the returned pointer for NULL to detect allocation failure.
The object must later be released with fido_credman_metadata_free.

functions.name: fido_credman_rk_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new container for resident credentials (RKs) retrieved from a device.
requirements: Caller must check for NULL to detect allocation failure.
The resulting object must be freed with fido_credman_rk_free.
Populate it via fido_credman_get_dev_rk before reading entries.

functions.name: fido_credman_rp_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new container for relying party (RP) entries retrieved from a device.
requirements: Check for NULL on allocation failure.
Free with fido_credman_rp_free when done.
Populate via fido_credman_get_dev_rp before accessing entries.

functions.name: fido_credman_del_dev_rk
functions.signature: int fido_credman_del_dev_rk(fido_dev_t *, const unsigned char *, size_t, const char *);
functions.description: Deletes a resident credential from a device, given its credential ID (binary) and optional PIN/authorization parameter. Returns a libfido2 error code (see fido/err.h).
requirements: The fido_dev_t pointer must refer to an opened/initialized FIDO device ready for credential management operations.
The credential ID buffer pointer must be non-NULL, and its size parameter must match the credential ID length for the target credential.
The PIN/authorization string parameter requirements are not specified here; it may need to be provided depending on device policy.
Caller must check the integer return value and handle errors per fido/err.h.
Do not pass invalid or out-of-range buffer lengths; doing so can cause the operation to fail.

functions.name: fido_credman_get_dev_metadata
functions.description: Populates a metadata object with resident credential counts (existing and remaining) from the device. Returns a libfido2 status code.
requirements: Device must be open/initialized for credential management.
The metadata object must be a valid instance created by fido_credman_metadata_new.
The PIN/authorization parameter usage is unspecified here; provide if required by the device.
Caller must check and handle the returned status code.
The metadata object must remain valid for the duration of the call and until the caller reads the results.

functions.name: fido_credman_get_dev_rk
functions.signature: int fido_credman_get_dev_rk(fido_dev_t *, const char *, fido_credman_rk_t *, const char *);
functions.description: Retrieves resident credentials for the specified relying party ID from the device and populates the provided RK container. Returns a libfido2 status code.
requirements: The device must be an open/initialized fido_dev_t supporting RK management.
The rp_id string must identify the relying party whose resident credentials are to be listed; format specifics are not detailed here (typically a domain string).
The RK container must be a valid instance created by fido_credman_rk_new and empty or ready to be overwritten.
A PIN/authorization string may be required by the device; the header does not specify whether NULL is allowed.
Caller must check the function's return code and handle errors.

functions.name: fido_credman_get_dev_rp
functions.description: Retrieves the list of relying parties for which the device has resident credentials and populates the provided RP container. Returns a libfido2 status code.
requirements: Device must be open/initialized and support credential management.
The RP container must be a valid instance created by fido_credman_rp_new and ready to receive data.
A PIN/authorization string may be required by the device; unspecified here whether NULL is allowed.
Caller must check and handle the returned status code.

functions.name: fido_credman_set_dev_rk
functions.description: Stores or updates a resident credential on the device using the provided fido_cred_t object. Returns a libfido2 status code.
requirements: Device must be open/initialized and support setting resident credentials.
The fido_cred_t pointer must reference a properly initialized credential object prepared for resident storage; specifics are not provided in this header.
A PIN/authorization string may be required by the device; requirements are unspecified here.
Caller must check the return value and handle errors as per fido/err.h.

functions.name: fido_credman_rk_count
functions.description: Returns the number of resident credential entries currently populated in the given RK container.
requirements: The RK container must be a valid instance, typically populated via fido_credman_get_dev_rk before use.

functions.name: fido_credman_rp_count
functions.description: Returns the number of relying party entries currently populated in the given RP container.
requirements: The RP container must be a valid instance, typically populated via fido_credman_get_dev_rp before use.

functions.name: fido_credman_rp_id_hash_len
functions.description: Returns the length in bytes of the RP ID hash for the RP entry at the given index in an RP container. Use together with fido_credman_rp_id_hash_ptr.
requirements: The RP container must be valid and populated.
The index must be < fido_credman_rp_count(container).
Use the returned length to bound access to the buffer returned by fido_credman_rp_id_hash_ptr at the same index.

functions.name: fido_credman_rk_existing
functions.description: Returns the number of resident credentials currently stored on the device, as recorded in the provided metadata object.
requirements: The metadata object must have been populated via fido_credman_get_dev_metadata before calling.

functions.name: fido_credman_rk_remaining
functions.description: Returns the number of remaining resident credential slots on the device, as recorded in the provided metadata object.
requirements: The metadata object must have been populated via fido_credman_get_dev_metadata before calling.

functions.name: fido_credman_metadata_free
functions.description: Frees a metadata object previously allocated with fido_credman_metadata_new and sets the caller's pointer to NULL.
requirements: Pass the address of a pointer returned by fido_credman_metadata_new (or NULL).

functions.name: fido_credman_rk_free
functions.description: Frees an RK container created by fido_credman_rk_new and sets the caller's pointer to NULL.
requirements: Pass the address of a pointer returned by fido_credman_rk_new (or NULL).
Do not access entries after freeing; the container becomes invalid.

functions.name: fido_credman_rp_free
functions.description: Frees an RP container created by fido_credman_rp_new and sets the caller's pointer to NULL.
requirements: Pass the address of a pointer returned by fido_credman_rp_new (or NULL).
Do not access entries after freeing; the container becomes invalid.

functions.name: fido_bio_template_name
functions.description: Returns the human-readable name associated with a biometric template. Used to read a template’s display/name string after it has been populated by the device or set by the caller.

functions.name: fido_bio_template

functions.name: fido_bio_template_id_ptr
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the raw identifier bytes of a biometric template. Use together with fido_bio_template_id_len to read the ID.
requirements: Argument must be a valid, initialized fido_bio_template_t.

The returned pointer is to internal storage owned by the template; do not free or modify it. Valid while the template object lives.

functions.name: fido_bio_info_new

functions.name: fido_bio_template_array_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new (initially empty) container for biometric templates.
requirements: Caller must check for NULL return to detect allocation failure.
The returned object must be released with fido_bio_template_array_free(&ptr).

functions.name: fido_bio_template_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new biometric template object for holding an ID and optional name. Often used as input/output for enrollment and management APIs.
requirements: Caller must check for NULL return to detect allocation failure.
The returned object must be released with fido_bio_template_free(&ptr).

functions.name: fido_bio_dev_enroll_begin

functions.description: Continues an ongoing biometric enrollment by requesting another sample. Updates the enrollment status structure with remaining samples and last status.
requirements: Device pointer must refer to an open/usable fido_dev_t (inferred).

functions.name: fido_bio_dev_enroll_remove

functions.description: Removes a biometric template from the device, identified by the provided template’s ID.

template must be a valid fido_bio_template_t containing a valid template ID.

Caller must check the returned int status and handle errors.

functions.name: fido_bio_dev_get_info
functions.description: Retrieves biometric capability/parameter information from the device and populates the provided info object.
requirements: Device pointer must refer to an open/usable fido_dev_t (inferred).
info must be a valid fido_bio_info_t allocated by fido_bio_info_new.
Caller must check the returned int status and handle errors before reading fields via accessors.

functions.name: fido_bio_dev_get_template_array
functions.description: Retrieves the set of biometric templates stored on the device and populates the provided template array.
requirements: Device pointer must refer to an open/usable fido_dev_t (inferred).
array must be a valid fido_bio_template_array_t allocated by fido_bio_template_array_new.
The PIN parameter may be required by the device; pass NULL or a NUL-terminated string as appropriate (exact policy unknown).

functions.name: fido_bio_dev_set_template_name
functions.signature: int fido_bio_dev_set_template_name(fido_dev_t *, const fido_bio_template_t *, const char *);

functions.name: fido_bio_template_set_name

requirements: template must be a valid fido_bio_template_t.
name must be a NUL-terminated string; encoding/length limits are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: fido_bio_template_array_count
functions.description: Returns the number of populated template entries currently present in the template array.

functions.name: fido_bio_template_id_len
functions.description: Returns the length in bytes of the template’s identifier data accessible via fido_bio_template_id_ptr.

functions.name: fido_bio_enroll_last_status

functions.name: fido_bio_enroll_remaining_samples

functions.name: fido_bio_info_type

requirements: info must be a valid, initialized fido_bio_info_t populated by fido_bio_dev_get_info.

functions.name: fido_bio_enroll_free

functions.name: fido_bio_info_free

functions.name: fido_bio_template_array_free
functions.description: Frees a fido_bio_template_array_t object (and any owned entries) and sets the caller’s pointer to NULL. Safe to call with a NULL pointer or a pointer to NULL.
requirements: Pass the address of a fido_bio_template_array_t* previously returned by fido_bio_template_array_new (or NULL).

functions.name: fido_bio_template_free
functions.description: Frees a fido_bio_template_t object and sets the caller’s pointer to NULL. Safe to call with a NULL pointer or a pointer to NULL.
requirements: Pass the address of a fido_bio_template_t* previously returned by fido_bio_template_new (or NULL).

functions.name: fido_assert_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new, empty FIDO assertion object. Use to prepare parameters for getting or verifying assertions.

functions.name: fido_cred_new

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for raw public key bytes suited for multiple stubs:
# - es256_pk_from_ptr: expect uncompressed P-256 point -> 65 bytes: 0x04 || X(32) || Y(32)
# - es384_pk_from_ptr: expect uncompressed P-384 point -> 97 bytes: 0x04 || X(48) || Y(48)
# - eddsa_pk_from_ptr: Ed25519 (32 bytes) or Ed448 (57 bytes)
# - rs256_pk_from_ptr: serialized RSA public key; library format is unspecified.
#   We will provide simple DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo (SPKI) or RSAPublicKey (PKCS#1) like encodings,
#   but to keep it self-contained and deterministic, we build a plausible PKCS#1 RSAPublicKey:
#   SEQ { n INTEGER (256 bytes), e INTEGER (3 bytes: 0x01 0x00 0x01) } wrapped in basic DER.
#   Some implementations accept raw concatenation n||e; we also produce that variant occasionally.
#
# The fuzzer harness feeds a single FUZZ_PARAM_STR buffer to each stub; we therefore produce one
# buffer per call. To increase useful coverage across different stubs, we randomly choose one of the
# valid encodings above per generate() invocation. All choices are valid encodings for at least one
# target stub and within 4096 bytes.

_DEF_EXPONENT = b"\x01\x00\x01"  # 65537


def _randbytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # rng.random() doesn't give bytes; use getrandbits for determinism under seed
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _int_to_der_integer(i_bytes: bytes) -> bytes:
    # DER INTEGER: ensure positive, add leading 0x00 if high bit set
    if len(i_bytes) == 0:
        i_bytes = b"\x00"
    # strip leading zeros to minimal encoding, but keep at least one byte
    i_bytes = i_bytes.lstrip(b"\x00") or b"\x00"
    if i_bytes[0] & 0x80:
        i_bytes = b"\x00" + i_bytes
    return b"\x02" + _der_len(len(i_bytes)) + i_bytes


def _der_len(n: int) -> bytes:
    if n < 0x80:
        return bytes([n])
    # long form
    tmp = []
    v = n
    while v > 0:
        tmp.append(v & 0xFF)
        v >>= 8
    tmp.reverse()
    return bytes([0x80 | len(tmp)]) + bytes(tmp)


def _der_sequence(payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    return b"\x30" + _der_len(len(payload)) + payload


def _gen_ec_uncompressed(rng: random.Random, coord_len: int) -> bytes:
    # 0x04 || X || Y with uniformly random field elements (does not guarantee on-curve, but format-valid)
    return b"\x04" + _randbytes(rng, coord_len) + _randbytes(rng, coord_len)


def _gen_ed25519(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # 32 random bytes is format-correct for many APIs expecting raw Ed25519 public key
    return _randbytes(rng, 32)


def _gen_ed448(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return _randbytes(rng, 57)


def _gen_rsa_pkcs1_der(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Generate a 2048-bit modulus n (256 bytes) and exponent e=65537
    n = bytearray(_randbytes(rng, 256))
    # Ensure n is odd and top bit set to look like a 2048-bit positive integer
    n[0] |= 0x80
    n[-1] |= 0x01
    der_n = _int_to_der_integer(bytes(n))
    der_e = _int_to_der_integer(_DEF_EXPONENT)
    return _der_sequence(der_n + der_e)


def _gen_rsa_raw_ne(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Raw concatenation n||e: 256-byte n followed by 3-byte e (65537)
    n = bytearray(_randbytes(rng, 256))
    n[0] |= 0x80
    n[-1] |= 0x01
    return bytes(n) + _DEF_EXPONENT


def _pick(rng: random.Random, items: List[Tuple[str, bytes]]) -> bytes:
    # Weighted choice: prefer commonly successful sizes to improve valid-path coverage
    # items is list of (name, data) but name unused; keep for readability if extended
    idx = rng.randrange(len(items))
    return items[idx][1]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build candidate buffers
    candidates: List[Tuple[str, bytes]] = []

    # ES256: 65 bytes
    candidates.append(("ec_p256", _gen_ec_uncompressed(rng, 32)))

    # ES384: 97 bytes
    candidates.append(("ec_p384", _gen_ec_uncompressed(rng, 48)))

    # Ed25519 and Ed448 raw
    candidates.append(("ed25519", _gen_ed25519(rng)))
    candidates.append(("ed448", _gen_ed448(rng)))

    # RSA encodings suitable for rs256_pk_from_ptr
    candidates.append(("rsa_pkcs1_der", _gen_rsa_pkcs1_der(rng)))
    candidates.append(("rsa_raw_ne", _gen_rsa_raw_ne(rng)))

    buf = _pick(rng, candidates)

    # Ensure size cap and non-empty buffer
    if not buf:
        buf = b"\x00"
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        buf = buf[:4096]
    return buf

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: PIN string (NUL-terminated C-string expected by the fuzz target wrappers)
# Goals for interesting, yet valid PINs:
# - Vary lengths (short, typical, long) within reasonable device policies
# - Vary character sets: digits only, alnum, with symbols, mixed case
# - Include edge cases commonly allowed by devices: leading/trailing spaces, repeated chars
# - Provide multiple candidate strings in one buffer so multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls can
#   consume them sequentially from the same underlying input corpus.
#
# Buffer format we produce:
# - A concatenation of multiple C strings separated by '\0'.
# - Ends with an extra '\0' to be safe.
# This maps well to fuzz harnesses that pick substrings or split on NUL boundaries.
#
# Size cap: <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

SYMBOLS = "!@#$%^&*()-_=+[]{}:;,./?"  # common ASCII punctuation allowed by many authenticators
PRINTABLE_NO_WS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + SYMBOLS
DIGITS = string.digits
ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits

COMMON_PINS = [
    "0000",
    "1111",
    "1234",
    "9999",
    "000000",
    "123456",
    "654321",
    "112233",
    "00000000",
    "12345678",
    # Typical policy-compliant examples
    "P@ssw0rd",
    "CorrectHorseBatteryStaple1!",
    "letmein123",
    "Pin-Code-2025",
]

# Some RP IDs for functions that expect non-empty domain-like strings (when used as PIN alternative)
RANDOM_DOMAIN_LABELS = [
    "example.com",
    "webauthn.test",
    "login.corp",
    "intranet.local",
    "service.example",
]


def _rand_choice(rnd: random.Random, charset: str, n: int) -> str:
    return "".join(rnd.choice(charset) for _ in range(n))


def _gen_digit_pin(rnd: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    return _rand_choice(rnd, DIGITS, length)


def _gen_alnum_pin(rnd: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    return _rand_choice(rnd, ALNUM, length)


def _gen_symbol_pin(rnd: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    # ensure at least one symbol and one digit where possible
    if length <= 2:
        base = _rand_choice(rnd, PRINTABLE_NO_WS, length)
        return base
    sym = rnd.choice(SYMBOLS)
    dig = rnd.choice(DIGITS)
    rest = _rand_choice(rnd, string.ascii_letters + DIGITS, length - 2)
    s = list(rest + sym + dig)
    rnd.shuffle(s)
    return "".join(s)


def _maybe_add_spaces(rnd: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Some devices allow spaces; include leading/trailing/inner spaces occasionally
    mode = rnd.randrange(0, 5)
    if mode == 0:
        return s
    if mode == 1:
        return " " + s
    if mode == 2:
        return s + " "
    if mode == 3:
        return " " + s + " "
    # insert a space somewhere inside if length permits
    if s:
        i = rnd.randrange(0, len(s))
        return s[:i] + " " + s[i:]
    return s


def _cap_length(s: str, max_len: int) -> str:
    if len(s) <= max_len:
        return s
    return s[:max_len]


def _unique_append(out: List[bytes], s: str) -> None:
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore') + b"\x00"
    if b not in out:
        out.append(b)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Include a curated set of common pins
    for s in COMMON_PINS:
        _unique_append(parts, s)

    # 2) Generate a range of lengths to hit device policy edges
    # Typical min 4, common 6-8, upper-bound around 63-128 depending on device.
    lengths = set([4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 32, 64, 80, 100, 128])
    # Add a couple random lengths in 4..128
    for _ in range(6):
        lengths.add(rnd.randint(4, 128))

    # 3) For each length, synthesize several styles
    for L in sorted(lengths):
        # digits only
        _unique_append(parts, _gen_digit_pin(rnd, L))
        # alphanumeric
        _unique_append(parts, _gen_alnum_pin(rnd, L))
        # with symbols
        _unique_append(parts, _gen_symbol_pin(rnd, L))
        # maybe with spaces
        _unique_append(parts, _maybe_add_spaces(rnd, _gen_symbol_pin(rnd, L)))

    # 4) Repetition and patterns that are still valid
    for ch in ['0', '1', 'a', 'A', 'x', 'Z', '!']:
        for L in [4, 6, 8, 12, 20, 32]:
            _unique_append(parts, ch * L)

    # 5) Mixed-case + digits + symbols combos
    for _ in range(20):
        L = rnd.randint(6, 48)
        s = _gen_symbol_pin(rnd, L)
        s = _maybe_add_spaces(rnd, s)
        _unique_append(parts, s)

    # 6) Include some domain-like strings for stubs that sometimes use FUZZ_PARAM_STR for paths/rpids
    for dom in RANDOM_DOMAIN_LABELS:
        _unique_append(parts, dom)
        # add subdomains
        _unique_append(parts, _cap_length(f"api.{dom}", 128))
        _unique_append(parts, _cap_length(f"auth.{dom}", 128))

    # 7) Short strings including empty-like but still non-empty (since some stubs guard empty)
    for s in ["1", "12", "abc", "A1!", " pin "]:
        _unique_append(parts, s)

    # Assemble within MAX_TOTAL budget
    out = b""
    rnd.shuffle(parts)
    for p in parts:
        if len(out) + len(p) > MAX_TOTAL - 1:
            break
        out += p

    # Ensure final double NUL terminator to be safe
    if not out.endswith(b"\x00\x00"):
        out += b"\x00"

    return out

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: domain name (RP ID)
# We generate valid-looking RP IDs (DNS-like), including:
# - plain domains with common TLDs
# - subdomains of varying depth
# - punycode-like labels (xn--...)
# - numeric labels and mixed case (case-insensitive per DNS)
# - longest label and near-max overall length while staying <= 253 chars
# - single-label hosts are technically allowed in some contexts, but WebAuthn RP IDs
#   are domain-like; we still generate at least two labels to favor validity.
# We keep total size <= 4096 as required.

COMMON_TLDS = [
    "com", "net", "org", "io", "dev", "app", "edu", "gov", "co", "us",
    "uk", "de", "fr", "jp", "cn", "au", "ca", "info", "me", "tech",
]

ALNUM = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits
ALNUM_MIXED = string.ascii_letters + string.digits


def _label_random(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 20, allow_mixed_case: bool = True) -> str:
    # DNS label rules: 1-63 chars, letters/digits/hyphen, cannot start/end with hyphen.
    lmin = max(1, min_len)
    lmax = min(63, max_len)
    n = rng.randint(lmin, lmax)
    # ensure first and last are alnum; middle can include '-'
    charset_mid = (ALNUM_MIXED if allow_mixed_case else string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) + "-"
    charset_edge = (ALNUM_MIXED if allow_mixed_case else string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits)
    if n == 1:
        return rng.choice(charset_edge)
    s = [rng.choice(charset_edge)]
    for _ in range(n - 2):
        s.append(rng.choice(charset_mid))
    s.append(rng.choice(charset_edge))
    return "".join(s)


def _label_punycode_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a punycode-like ascii label starting with xn--
    core_len = rng.randint(1, 20)
    core_charset = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-"
    core = "".join(rng.choice(core_charset) for _ in range(core_len))
    # ensure not ending with '-'
    if core and core[-1] == '-':
        core = core[:-1] + rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits)
    return "xn--" + core


def _make_domain(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose a pattern
    pattern = rng.randint(0, 8)

    # Base TLD selection
    tld = rng.choice(COMMON_TLDS)

    labels: List[str] = []

    if pattern == 0:
        # simple: sub + domain + tld
        labels = [
            _label_random(rng, 3, 12),
            _label_random(rng, 3, 12),
            tld,
        ]
    elif pattern == 1:
        # deep subdomain (3-5 labels before TLD)
        depth = rng.randint(3, 5)
        labels = [_label_random(rng, 1, 10) for _ in range(depth)] + [tld]
    elif pattern == 2:
        # include a long label near 63 chars
        long_label = _label_random(rng, 30, 63, allow_mixed_case=False)
        labels = [long_label, _label_random(rng, 3, 10, allow_mixed_case=False), tld]
    elif pattern == 3:
        # punycode-like label at front
        labels = [_label_punycode_like(rng), _label_random(rng, 3, 12, allow_mixed_case=False), tld]
    elif pattern == 4:
        # numeric-heavy labels
        num_label = ''.join(rng.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 10)))
        alnum_label = _label_random(rng, 2, 15)
        # ensure numeric label doesn't start/end with '-' (it won't)
        labels = [alnum_label, num_label, tld]
    elif pattern == 5:
        # mixed case labels
        labels = [
            _label_random(rng, 2, 15, allow_mixed_case=True),
            _label_random(rng, 2, 15, allow_mixed_case=True),
            tld,
        ]
    elif pattern == 6:
        # very long domain near 253 chars (sum of labels + dots <= 253)
        # build labels until we approach the limit
        remaining = 253
        # reserve for tld and final dot count; start with tld at end
        tld_label = tld
        labels = []
        def can_add(lbls: List[str], new: str) -> bool:
            total = sum(len(x) for x in lbls) + len(new) + len(tld_label) + (len(lbls) + 1)  # dots between labels
            return total <= 253
        while True:
            # Prefer 10-20 char labels to reach near limit
            candidate = _label_random(rng, 5, 20, allow_mixed_case=False)
            if can_add(labels, candidate):
                labels.append(candidate)
                # try to add more; limit length of list to avoid huge
                if len(labels) > 8 and rng.random() < 0.3:
                    break
            else:
                break
        labels.append(tld_label)
        if len(labels) < 2:
            labels = [_label_random(rng, 3, 12), tld]
    elif pattern == 7:
        # common developer domains
        labels = [rng.choice(["api", "auth", "login", "id", "account", "cdn", "static"]),
                  _label_random(rng, 3, 12, allow_mixed_case=False), tld]
    else:
        # two-label domain
        labels = [_label_random(rng, 3, 20, allow_mixed_case=False), tld]

    domain = ".".join(labels)

    # Ensure overall length constraints and no empty labels
    # If too long (unlikely except pattern 6 edge), trim first label
    if len(domain) > 253:
        parts = domain.split('.')
        # Trim the first non-TLD label to fit
        excess = len(domain) - 253
        for i in range(len(parts) - 1):
            if len(parts[i]) > 1 and excess > 0:
                trim = min(excess, len(parts[i]) - 1)
                parts[i] = parts[i][:-trim]
                break
        domain = ".".join(parts)
    # Lowercase for normalization in most contexts
    return domain.lower()


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Randomly choose how many RP IDs to emit; many stubs take a single string,
    # others may read multiple via FUZZ_PARAM_STR sequences. We produce one RP ID
    # per buffer; harness will request more as needed.
    rp = _make_domain(rng)

    # Also include possibility to return an empty-but-non-empty-safe fallback by ensuring len>=1.
    if not rp:
        rp = "example.com"

# Data type: credential ID (binary)
# Buffer delivered to FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls as multiple length-prefixed strings.
# Layout:
# [count:u8] then for each entry: [len:u16_be][bytes]
# Entries:
# 0: device path (non-empty)
# 1: credential id (<=512, non-empty)
# 2: optional PIN (may be empty)
# 3: credential id for largeblob ops (<=256, non-empty)
# 4: largeblob data (<=1024, non-empty)

_MAX_TOTAL = 4096
_ALPHA = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789-_"


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(max(0, n)))


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    if n <= 0:
        return b""
    return bytes(rng.choice(_ALPHA) for _ in range(n))


def _make_device_path(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choices = []
    vid = rng.randrange(0x0001, 0xffff)
    pid = rng.randrange(0x0001, 0xffff)
    choices.append(f"hid:vid_{vid:04x}&pid_{pid:04x}".encode())
    choices.append(b"/dev/hidraw" + str(rng.randrange(0, 64)).encode())
    choices.append((r"\\\\?\hid#vid_%04x&pid_%04x#%08x" % (vid, pid, rng.randrange(1, 1<<32))).encode())
    choices.append(b"fido://device/" + _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randrange(4, 12)))
    return rng.choice(choices)


def _make_credential_id(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Select interesting length within [1, max_len]
    candidates = [
        1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 80, 96, 112, 128, 160, 192,
        max(1, max_len // 4), max(1, max_len // 2), max(1, (3 * max_len) // 4),
        max(1, max_len - 1), max_len,
    ]
    lens = sorted({l for l in candidates if 1 <= l <= max_len})
    L = rng.choice(lens)

    b = bytearray()
    pattern = rng.randrange(0, 6)
    if pattern == 0:
        b.extend(_rand_bytes(rng, L))
    elif pattern == 1:
        prefix = bytes([0xA1 | (rng.randrange(1, 4))])  # small CBOR map-ish byte
        rest = _rand_bytes(rng, max(0, L - len(prefix)))
        b.extend(prefix)
        b.extend(rest)
    elif pattern == 2:
        kh_len = max(1, L - 1)
        b.append(kh_len & 0xFF)
        b.extend(_rand_bytes(rng, kh_len))
        if len(b) < L:
            b.extend(_rand_bytes(rng, L - len(b)))
    elif pattern == 3:
        asc_len = min(L, rng.randrange(1, min(20, L) + 1))
        b.extend(_rand_ascii(rng, asc_len))
        if len(b) < L:
            b.extend(_rand_bytes(rng, L - len(b)))
    elif pattern == 4:
        aaguid_len = min(16, L)
        b.extend(_rand_bytes(rng, aaguid_len))
        if len(b) < L:
            b.extend(_rand_bytes(rng, L - len(b)))
    else:
        half = max(1, L // 2)
        c1 = _rand_bytes(rng, min(half, max(1, L - 3)))
        c2 = _rand_bytes(rng, max(0, L - (2 + len(c1))))
        inner = struct.pack(">B", len(c1) & 0xFF) + c1 + c2
        if len(inner) < L:
            inner += _rand_bytes(rng, L - len(inner))
        b.extend(inner[:L])
    return bytes(b[:L])


def _make_pin(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        return b""  # optional empty
    length = rng.randrange(4, 17)
    return _rand_ascii(rng, length)


def _make_largeblob_data(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Choose non-empty length
    candidates = [1, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, max_len]
    lens = sorted({l for l in candidates if 1 <= l <= max_len})
    L = rng.choice(lens)

    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return _rand_bytes(rng, L)
    else:
        # Ensure head length range is valid
        head_max = min(64, L)
        head_min = 1 if L >= 1 else 0
        head_len = rng.randrange(head_min, head_max + 1) if head_max >= head_min and head_min > 0 else 0
        head_len = min(head_len, L)
        head = _rand_ascii(rng, head_len)
        tail = _rand_bytes(rng, L - len(head))
        return head + tail


def _pack_length_prefixed(entries: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    out.append(len(entries) & 0xFF)
    for e in entries:
        out.extend(struct.pack(">H", len(e)))
        out.extend(e)
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    dev_path = _make_device_path(rng)
    cid_general = _make_credential_id(rng, 512)
    pin = _make_pin(rng)
    cid_largeblob = _make_credential_id(rng, 256)
    lb_data = _make_largeblob_data(rng, 1024)

    entries = [dev_path, cid_general, pin, cid_largeblob, lb_data]
    buf = _pack_length_prefixed(entries)

    return buf[:_MAX_TOTAL]

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Data type: "identifier bytes" — opaque binary identifiers for things like biometric templates,
# authenticator data, signatures, attestation elements, clientDataHash, credential IDs, etc.
# The fuzzer stubs request FUZZ_PARAM_STR for many buffers. We should return a bytes blob that,
# when split/consumed sequentially by FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned ...), yields valid data:
# - Non-empty buffers where required (many stubs bail on empty strings)
# - Reasonable sizes (e.g., clientDataHash requires 32 bytes; user ids bounded to 256 by stub)
# - Authenticator data-like structures to satisfy parsers when used
#
# Strategy:
# Construct a self-describing container with multiple concatenated TLV chunks. The harness
# will slice them in order via FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls. We pack various chunks that look like:
# - Generic identifier bytes (length 16, 32, 64, 128)
# - A well-formed WebAuthn authenticatorData (rpIdHash[32] + flags + sigCount[4] + attested credential)
# - Signature-like blobs (DER-ish header + random)
# - Attestation statement CBOR-ish bytes (not required to be valid CBOR, but non-empty arbitrary)
# - Strings usable as device path and PIN (ASCII subset)
# The fuzzer only needs non-empty buffers and reasonable lengths; it does not verify CBOR.
#
# We also include a 32-byte block explicitly for clientDataHash requests.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Helper to make random printable ASCII string bytes
def rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    l = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789._-/@+"
    return bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(l))

# Build a CTAP/WebAuthn-like authenticatorData buffer:
# rpIdHash(32) | flags(1) | signCount(4) | optionally attested credential data
# For robustness, always include at least rpIdHash+flags+signCount and sometimes attested block.

def build_authdata(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    rp_id_hash = rng.randbytes(32)
    # Flags: UP(0x01), UV(0x04), AT(0x40) maybe set; randomize but ensure some bits set
    flags = (1 if rng.random() < 0.8 else 0) | (4 if rng.random() < 0.5 else 0) | (0x40 if rng.random() < 0.6 else 0)
    sigcount = rng.randrange(0, 1 << 24)
    buf = bytearray()
    buf += rp_id_hash
    buf.append(flags)
    buf += struct.pack(">I", sigcount)
    if flags & 0x40:
        # attestedCredentialData: AAGUID(16) | credIdLen(2) | credId | pubKey(COSE-ish)
        aaguid = rng.randbytes(16)
        # Credential ID length between 16 and 64
        cred_len = rng.randint(16, 64)
        cred_id = rng.randbytes(cred_len)
        # Fake COSE key map (CBOR-like) but just opaque bytes with typical size 64-120
        pk_len = rng.randint(64, 120)
        pubkey = rng.randbytes(pk_len)
        buf += aaguid
        buf += struct.pack(">H", cred_len)
        buf += cred_id
        buf += pubkey
    return bytes(buf)

# Build a DER-like ECDSA signature blob: SEQ | two INTEGERs lengths; but content can be arbitrary bytes

def build_der_like_sig(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    r_len = rng.randint(20, 33)
    s_len = rng.randint(20, 33)
    r_val = b"\x00" + rng.randbytes(r_len) if rng.random() < 0.5 else rng.randbytes(r_len)
    s_val = b"\x00" + rng.randbytes(s_len) if rng.random() < 0.5 else rng.randbytes(s_len)
    body = b"\x02" + bytes([len(r_val)]) + r_val + b"\x02" + bytes([len(s_val)]) + s_val
    seq = b"\x30" + bytes([len(body)]) + body
    return seq

# Simple TLV builder to concatenate multiple payloads with small headers, though consumer ignores headers.

def tlv(tag: int, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">BH", tag & 0xFF, len(data)) + data


def build_container(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    # 1) clientDataHash (32 bytes)
    chunks.append(tlv(1, rng.randbytes(32)))
    # 2) user id (length 8-64, bounded later by stub to 256)
    chunks.append(tlv(2, rng.randbytes(rng.randint(8, 64))))
    # 3) display name string (non-empty ascii)
    chunks.append(tlv(3, rand_ascii(rng, 6, 24)))
    # 4) name string (optional but we set it)
    chunks.append(tlv(4, rand_ascii(rng, 4, 20)))
    # 5) icon string (optional)
    chunks.append(tlv(5, rand_ascii(rng, 4, 20)))
    # 6) authenticator parsed authdata
    chunks.append(tlv(6, build_authdata(rng)))
    # 7) authenticator raw authdata (another variant)
    chunks.append(tlv(7, build_authdata(rng)))
    # 8) signature buffer (non-empty)
    chunks.append(tlv(8, build_der_like_sig(rng)))
    # 9) attestation statement bytes (arbitrary non-empty 40-120)
    chunks.append(tlv(9, rng.randbytes(rng.randint(40, 120))))
    # 10) device path string (non-empty ascii to open device)
    chunks.append(tlv(10, b"/dev/hidraw" + rand_ascii(rng, 1, 6)))
    # 11) PIN candidate (possibly empty per device policy, but we'll make non-empty printable)
    chunks.append(tlv(11, rand_ascii(rng, 4, 16)))
    # 12) biometric template ID (16-32 bytes typical opaque id)
    chunks.append(tlv(12, rng.randbytes(rng.randint(16, 32))))
    # 13) extra generic buffer to satisfy additional FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers
    for tag in range(20, 24):
        chunks.append(tlv(tag, rng.randbytes(rng.randint(12, 64))))

    blob = b"".join(chunks)
    if len(blob) > MAX_TOTAL:
        blob = blob[:MAX_TOTAL]
    return blob


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Python 3.10 random.Random has no randbytes; emulate for portability
    if not hasattr(rng, "randbytes"):
        def _rb(n: int) -> bytes:
            return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))
        setattr(rng, "randbytes", _rb)  # type: ignore
    data = build_container(rng)
    # Ensure non-empty and within 4096
    if not data:
        data = bytes([0])
    return data
